text:
nina: FYI rolled out response-pool-compression v1 to gen clusters (routes that return many candidate tokens).

nina: TL;DR: median latency same, p95 down ~11% for batched generation-heavy routes, and token compute units down ~22% on sampled workloads.

salvador: nice. short canary numbers?

nina: canary (1h): baseline p95 = 340ms -> v1 p95 = 302ms, p50 = 58ms -> 57ms. avg token compute per request -22%. pool reuse rate 12% -> 54%.

jo: how does compression work? any accuracy impact?

nina: we compress intermediate response pools (shared KV slices + logits) using a lightweight lossy transform tuned to keep top-k probabilities intact; then decompress on the fast-path for final sampling. QA rounds ran on core eval sets; no measurable quality regressions for top-1/top-5 on our checks.

kim: config flip?

nina: config snippet:
```
response_pool.compression.enabled = true
response_pool.compression.level = "lite"
response_pool.min_share_for_compress = 2
```

infra-bot: deploy: response-pool-compression-v1 promoted to default in region-us-west-2 at 2027-03-09T14:22:40Z :white_check_mark:

salvador: any incidents or gotchas?

nina: one tenant had high-candidate-variance causing extra decompress CPU; we auto-pinned them to no-compression for 10m and created ticket #7101 to add heuristics. small memory uptick on older nodes guarded by autoscaler.

jo: alerts/dashboards?

nina: dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.com/d/response-pool/compression-v1 
runbook: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/response-pool-compression 
alerts: response_pool.decompress.cpu.p95 and response_pool.share.rate.drop. safety fallback: if compression leads to >3% quality delta on eval hooks for 30m, auto-fallback to legacy.

kim: customers need to change anything?

nina: no API changes. policy note: default response_pool policy for gen routes with >1 candidate is now "compress-lite"; teams needing byte-for-byte determinism can opt out via `route.response_pool = "no-compress"`.

salvador: please draft a short blurb for #announcements. follow-ups: #7101 (decompress heuristics), #7102 (opt-out telemetry), #7103 (announce blurb).

nina: closing thread  ping if you see >5% token-cost regressions.
